args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploying checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. (The v2.3.1-rc build was also unhealthy in staging.) I rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is about 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it.

trace.final:
checkout-api has been rolled back to v2.3.0 in all production regions, and it's healthy again.

- **The problem:** v2.3.1 was the latest release, and it was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west with an error rate of about 18%. Its release candidate, v2.3.1-rc, was also failing in staging.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. All three regions now run it. The service passes health checks and the error rate has dropped to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** I opened **INC-0001** (SEV2) for checkout-api, which paged the on-call engineer. It describes the failure, the rollback and the result, and says the cause of the v2.3.1 failure should be found before it's deployed again.

The rollback went to a version that was already healthy in production, so it didn't need change-manager approval.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
